title: Oxidation Orbit: States and Half-Equations
welcome_lead: Track electrons with oxidation states and balance half-equations.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on oxidation states and half-equations.
final_note: You traced electrons through redox space.

concepts.def: A value showing the degree of oxidation of an atom.
Tendency of a half-cell to gain electrons, measured against hydrogen.
Two half-cells producing an EMF from a redox reaction.
Using electricity to drive a non-spontaneous redox reaction.
Show what happens at each electrode.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Free element = 0. Group 1 = +1, Group 2 = +2. H = +1 (-1 in hydrides). O = -2 (-1 in peroxides). F = -1. Ions sum to charge.

Example: in KMnO4: K = +1, O = -2 × 4 = -8, so Mn = +7. In Cr2O7^2-: Cr = +6 each.

Steps: balance atom of interest, add H2O for O, add H+ for H, add e- to balance charge.

Example reduction of MnO4-: MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn^2+ + 4H2O.

Multiply each half-equation so e- cancel. Add together; cancel duplicate species.

Example: Fe^2+ -> Fe^3+ + e- × 5 added to MnO4- reduction gives MnO4- + 8H+ + 5Fe^2+ -> Mn^2+ + 5Fe^3+ + 4H2O.

mcqs.q: Oxidation state of Mn in MnO4-?

options: Loss of electrons
Gain of electrons
Gain of protons
Loss of protons

mcqs.q: What is reduction in terms of electrons?
options: Gain of electrons (the oxidation number is reduced).
The oxidation state of an atom is always equal to the number of electrons it has.
Reduction means losing oxygen and oxidation means gaining oxygen — full stop.
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.

mcqs.q: Is the oxidation state of an atom the same as its actual charge?
options: The oxidation state of an atom is always equal to the number of electrons it has.
The oxidation state of an atom is exactly equal to its real ionic charge in every compound.
Not necessarily — oxidation state is an accounting tool assuming all bonds are fully ionic; real charge is usually smaller.
The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.

mcqs.q: In a standard hydrogen electrode used as a reference, what is the assigned electrode potential?
options: The standard hydrogen electrode actually has zero potential because hydrogen has no charge.
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.
The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.
Exactly 0 V by convention — all other electrode potentials are measured relative to it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reduction”?
options: Species that gets reduced; takes e-.
Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain.
Equation showing electron transfer only.
Gain of electrons; ox state decreases.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “OIL RIG”?
options: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain.
Loss of electrons; ox state increases.
Equation showing electron transfer only.
Gain of electrons; ox state decreases.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Oxidation”?
options: Gain of electrons; ox state decreases.
Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain.
Loss of electrons; ox state increases.
Equation showing electron transfer only.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reducing agent”?
options: Equation showing electron transfer only.
Species that gets oxidised; gives e-.
Gain of electrons; ox state decreases.
Species that gets reduced; takes e-.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Half-equation”?
options: Loss of electrons; ox state increases.
Equation showing electron transfer only.
Species that gets reduced; takes e-.
Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Oxidising agent”?
options: Equation showing electron transfer only.
Species that gets reduced; takes e-.
Species that gets oxidised; gives e-.
Loss of electrons; ox state increases.
